chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are allies alongside the Sultan (ruling authority) by whom He defends His allies.'

key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِهِ: His allies (referring to the friends of God)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the Sultan and Allah's allies according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kulayni’s chapter on government workforce stipulations, this hadith elucidates the concept of 'Awliya al-Sultan' (allies of the ruler), suggesting that divine protection for the faithful is often mediated through established political structures. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that legitimate authority serves as a vessel for divine order, ensuring that the 'awliya' (friends of God) are safeguarded even amidst worldly governance.
